i0: Use a **reflexive pronoun** when the subject and the object are the **same** person: *I cut **myself**. She taught **herself** English.*
i1: Use ***each other*** when two or more people do something **to one another**: *They love **each other**.*
rrp-forms.t: Myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, themselves
rrp-forms.s: Use a **reflexive pronoun** when the **subject and object are the same**: *I hurt **myself**. They enjoyed **themselves**.*
rrp-forms.b1: Compare: *She looked at **her**.* (another woman) / *She looked at **herself**.* (in the mirror)
rrp-forms.b2: Spelling: singular *-self*, plural *-selves*. Say *himself* and *themselves* (not *hisself, theirselves*).
rrp-verbs.t: Enjoy yourself, help yourself, by myself; relax, feel, meet
rrp-verbs.s: Some verbs often take a reflexive pronoun: ***enjoy yourself, help yourself, behave yourself, introduce yourself***. Many verbs usually **don't** in English: *relax, feel, concentrate, meet, wash, get dressed*. ***By myself*** = alone.
rrp-verbs.b1: ***Enjoy*** needs an object: *Did you **enjoy yourself**? Did you **enjoy the party**?* (not *Did you enjoy?*)
rrp-verbs.b2: Use *wash, shave* and *get dressed* without *myself* unless you want to emphasise it: *I got up, **washed** and **got dressed**.*
rrp-each-other.s: Use ***each other*** (or ***one another***) when two or more people do something **to the other(s)**: *Ali and Sara love **each other**.* Compare: *They blamed **themselves*** (each blamed himself or herself) / *They blamed **each other*** (A blamed B, and B blamed A).
rrp-each-other.b0.0.0: *They blamed **themselves**.* (each one blamed himself or herself)
rrp-each-other.b0.0.1: *They blamed **each other**.* (A blamed B, B blamed A)
rrp-each-other.b2: ***One another*** means the same and is a little more formal: *The students helped **one another**.*
rrp-each-other.b3: Some verbs don't need *each other*: *They **met** in 2010. They **kissed**. They **got married**.*
x.rrp-each-other-s01: A tells B, B tells A: *each other*.
x.rrp-each-other-s02: A looked at B, B at A: *each other*.
x.rrp-verbs-b05: *Dress herself* = put on her own clothes.
q.rrp-each-other-b03: Which sentence means *A blamed B, and B blamed A*?
